findings_addressed.oracle: Exactly one ERROR record was emitted (real_error_only) before the window opened; the independent count oracle is the static knowledge that logger.error() was called exactly once, so after applying logging.ERROR filter the proxy must contain exactly 1 row.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/ui/log_viewer/_proxy.py filterAcceptsRow(), change `if record_level_int < self.min_level:` to `if record_level_int <= self.min_level:` — this would hide ERROR-level records too, making rowCount() == 0 instead of 1 and failing the assertion.

notes: Finding G0320: replaced `assert window.proxy.rowCount() >= 1` (weak existence, admitted zero-row no-op) with `assert window.proxy.rowCount() == 1` (pins exact count). The test emits exactly one ERROR record before the window opens; after applying logging.ERROR filter the proxy must show exactly one row. This is an independent oracle because: (1) the emit count is known statically (one logger.error() call), (2) the expected count is distinct from both the default state (0 before records arrive) and a no-op broken filter (0 or many). The prior assertions vis_levels == {'ERROR'} and event membership checks are retained as complementary gates.
